+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# AIDLC plugin — SessionStart compose hook (harness-agnostic).
+# Runs automatically when installed as a host plugin (Claude/Codex) or via
+# `aidlc plugin compose` (Kiro). Merges the plugin's stages, sensors, and tools
+# into the project's harness tree (.claude / .codex / .kiro) and recompiles the
+# stage graph so the orchestrator routes the new stages.
+#
+# Idempotent: safe to re-run on every session start (only copies + recompile).
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Plugin root: Claude sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT; Codex sets PLUGIN_ROOT (and aliases
+# CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT). Kiro's thin CLI passes AIDLC_PLUGIN_ROOT.
+PLUGIN_ROOT="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${PLUGIN_ROOT:-${AIDLC_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}}}"
+# Project dir: Claude sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; Codex does NOT (use PWD); Kiro's
+# CLI passes AIDLC_PROJECT_DIR.
+PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-${AIDLC_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}}"
+# Harness leaf dir (.claude / .codex / .kiro) — set per-harness by hooks.json /
+# the Kiro CLI. Default .claude for backward compatibility.
+HARNESS_LEAF="${AIDLC_HARNESS_DIR:-.claude}"
+HARNESS_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/$HARNESS_LEAF"
+
+if [ -z "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ]; then
+  echo "aidlc-plugin: plugin root env not set (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_ROOT/AIDLC_PLUGIN_ROOT); skipping" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Guard: only compose if this is an AIDLC project (has the graph compiler)
+if [ ! -f "$HARNESS_DIR/tools/aidlc-graph.ts" ]; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Resolve bun (the probe showed it may not be on bare PATH in hook context)
+BUN="${BUN:-}"
+if [ -z "$BUN" ]; then
+  if command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    BUN="bun"
+  elif [ -x "$HOME/.bun/bin/bun" ]; then
+    BUN="$HOME/.bun/bin/bun"
+  else
+    echo "aidlc-test-pro: bun not found; skipping compose" >&2
+    exit 0
+  fi
+fi
+
+# The harness-dir token substitution the packager applies to core .md prose.
+# Plugin .md files carry {{HARNESS_DIR}}; substitute it to the actual dir
+# (HARNESS_LEAF, resolved above) so composed stage/sensor prose is
+# harness-correct. Applied only to the files this plugin adds, never the tree.
+#
+# copy_and_substitute <src-dir> <dst-dir> — copy the tree, then substitute the
+# harness-dir token in every copied .md file.
+copy_and_substitute() {
+  local src="$1" dst="$2"
+  [ -d "$src" ] || return 0
+  cp -rn "$src"/* "$dst/" 2>/dev/null || cp -r "$src"/* "$dst/"
+  # substitute the token in the files we just copied (match by relative path)
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    local rel="${f#"$src"/}"
+    local target="$dst/$rel"
+    [ -f "$target" ] || continue
+    case "$target" in
+      *.md) sed -i "s|{{HARNESS_DIR}}|${HARNESS_LEAF}|g" "$target" ;;

discussion_comments.comment_body:
**BLOCKER:** `sed -i "s|...|...|g" "$target"` is the GNU form. BSD sed (macOS) requires an argument to `-i` and consumes the s-command string as the backup suffix, then fails parsing the filename as a script:

```
$ sed -i "s|{{HARNESS_DIR}}|.claude|g" test.md
sed: 2: "test.md
": undefined label 'est.md'   # exit 1
```

With `set -euo pipefail` (line 9) the hook aborts on the first `.md` file, before steps 4 (contributions), 5 (fragments), and 6 (recompile) run - so on macOS the plugin never composes. This is also why t188 fails 10/10 on Darwin.

Two levels of fix, deepest first:

**a) Pre-project at package time so substitution is off the hot path.**

To be clear on the design intent this rests on, since "install time" covers two different operations in the agreed model: PROJECTION (rendering the harness-neutral source into `.claude`/`.kiro`/`.codex` shape, including the `{{HARNESS_DIR}}` substitution) happens at PUBLISH time, once per harness - the harness is fixed by which store/repo you install from, never figured out at install, and each published artifact is a valid fetch-and-load host plugin. COMPOSITION (copying stages in, merging contributions into core stages, recompiling the graph) is the part that happens at INSTALL time via the SessionStart hook. This PR keeps composition at install time (correct) but also defers projection to install time: the emitted .md files still carry the literal `{{HARNESS_DIR}}` token (visible in `dist/plugins/test-pro/claude/stages/*.md` today) and the sed at this line is doing publish-time work on every user machine at every session start.

The fix: route plugin content through the packager's existing walk+substituteToken path (scripts/package.ts line 78) - emitPlugins already emits one tree per harness and knows `harnessLeaf`, so this is wiring, not new machinery. The emitted artifact then loads as-is for the common single-plugin case (the memoized fast path in the agreed model), and this sed disappears. Substitution machinery does still belong in the compose layer for the multi-plugin case - the design keeps the neutral source in the payload so compose can re-merge and re-project when more than one plugin contributes to the same stage - but that is the cold path, and it should be bun TS, not sed.

**b)** If install-time substitution must stay, move it into the bun compose layer per the summary comment: a single compose.ts doing `content.replaceAll("{{HARNESS_DIR}}", leaf)` + writeFileSync. Only as a stopgap, the portable shell form is `sed -i.bak ... && rm -f "$target.bak"`. (Same lines ship in all three emitted copies under dist/plugins/test-pro/*/hooks/, so a repackage is needed after the fix.)

discussion_comments.comment_body:
**BLOCKER** (same pattern at line 75 for tools/):

```sh
cp -rn "$src"/* "$dst/" 2>/dev/null || cp -r "$src"/* "$dst/"
```

The fallback defeats the no-clobber intent. On BSD cp (macOS) and GNU coreutils >= 9.2, `cp -n` exits 1 whenever it skips an existing file, so the `|| cp -r` branch fires deterministically on any name collision and overwrites the existing file. Verified locally:

```
cp -rn src dst   -> skips, exit 1
|| cp -r         -> overwrites: dst now has the plugin's copy
```

Line 75 copies straight into `$HARNESS_DIR/tools/`, so a plugin shipping a file named like a core tool (e.g. `aidlc-lib.ts`) would silently replace the framework's copy on every SessionStart.

Suggested fix, per the summary comment: do the copy in the bun compose.ts - walk the source tree and per file `if (!existsSync(dest)) cpSync(src, dest)`. That is both the no-clobber semantics this line wants and portable by construction. Whatever the fix, do not use `cp -n`'s exit code as a "nothing was skipped" signal - it means "something already existed" on the two most common cp implementations.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
`2>/dev/null || true` on all three bun calls means any failure (import error, malformed YAML, the regex SyntaxError from comment #6, disk full) is swallowed silently. The graph then compiles against stages missing their contributions — the workflow runs but with incomplete stages (missing produces/sensors/fragments) and no signal to the user.

Combined with apackeer's #6: a single regex throw in compose-fragments aborts all remaining fragments for that contribution file, `|| true` eats the exit, and the partial compose is invisible. `--doctor` doesn't verify compose integrity either.

If the fold to compose.ts happens, these become try/catch blocks that can at least log what failed to a health file (same pattern as `recordHookDrop` in the core hooks).
